original_question: For polygonal symplectic billiards, classify all polygons with the property that every symplectic billiard orbit is periodic.
target_in_paper: Serge Tabachnikov, Problem 3, Question 1: "Describe all such polygons," where the immediately preceding sentence defines "such polygons" as polygons for which all symplectic billiard orbits are periodic.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right topic (polygonal symplectic billiards), the right global periodicity property (every orbit is periodic), and the right task (to describe/classify exactly those polygons). This matches the paper’s intended open problem very closely.
missing_details: The paper’s setting is planar: the dynamics is on oriented chords of a polygon in the plane.
The polygonal setup used in the cited source [2] is convex polygons; non-convex polygons are mentioned as definable but are not the main scope of the classification problem.
The dynamical object should be named explicitly as the polygonal symplectic billiard map, not just 'orbits' in an informal sense.
The phase space is not all pairs of boundary points: the map is undefined when the head of the oriented chord is a vertex, and also when the tail and head lie on parallel sides.
To be fully stand-alone, periodicity should be stated as: every orbit of the polygonal symplectic billiard map on its phase space is periodic.

The paper says 'describe' rather than formally specifying a classification up to a particular equivalence relation; although affine equivalence is natural because the dynamics is affine-invariant, the open problem itself does not impose that as part of the statement.
refined_question: Describe all convex planar polygons P for which the polygonal symplectic billiard map T_P on its phase space of oriented chords of P (excluding the chords for which the map is undefined, such as those with head at a vertex or with endpoints on parallel sides) is fully periodic; that is, every orbit of T_P is periodic.
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:2110.10750 is not a conjecture or theorem but Serge Tabachnikov’s Problem 3, Question 1. The surrounding text first recalls the planar symplectic billiard reflection law, then says that polygonal symplectic billiards are defined similarly, and then asks to 'Describe all such polygons' after specifying that the target class is polygons for which all symplectic billiard orbits are periodic. To make that one-line question mathematically stand-alone, one must import the hidden setup from the cited polygonal symplectic billiards paper [2]: the main setting there is convex planar polygons, the map acts on oriented chords, and its phase space excludes the obvious singular cases where the reflection is not defined. I therefore kept the scope exactly on the fully periodic case and did not replace it by the neighboring question asking whether every polygon has at least one periodic orbit.
